findings.title: Journal search crashes (HTTP 500) on an apostrophe or quote; search term is interpolated into SQL
findings.where: GET /api/journal?q=... (backend/routers/journal.py list_entries); Journal page search box, plant detail journal load
findings.steps: Sign in. Open the Journal page and type a word containing an apostrophe, e.g. O'Neil (or any ' or "). Equivalent API: curl -G 'http://localhost:8790/api/journal' --data-urlencode "q=O'Neil".
findings.expected: The search runs and returns matching entries (or an empty list), with the quote treated as a literal character. Bad input should never cause a 5xx.
findings.actual: Server returns 500 Internal Server Error. The front end then shows the generic 'Could not load the journal.' alert and no results. Any plant whose name or a user who types a quote in search hits this.
findings.evidence: Code builds the WHERE clause with an f-string: clauses.append(f"(j.body LIKE '%{term}%' OR p.name LIKE '%{term}%')") and passes it to conn.execute with no parameterization. curl with q=O'Neil returned HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error'; q containing a quote consistently 500s while safe terms 200. This is also a SQL injection vector.

findings.title: Journal search treats % and _ as SQL LIKE wildcards instead of literal characters
findings.where: GET /api/journal?q=... (backend/routers/journal.py list_entries); Journal page search box
findings.steps: Sign in, open Journal page, search for a single '%' (or '_'). API: curl -G 'http://localhost:8790/api/journal' --data-urlencode 'q=%'.
findings.expected: Searching for '%' should match only entries that literally contain a percent sign (likely none), not every entry.
findings.actual: Searching '%' returns ALL entries (it is used as a LIKE wildcard), and '_' matches any single character. Results are misleading; a user searching for a literal % or _ can never find it.
findings.evidence: LIKE pattern is built by raw interpolation with no ESCAPE clause; curl with q=%25 returned the full entry list identical to no filter.

findings.title: Journal page load-error state offers no retry
findings.steps: Load the Journal page while the API is failing (e.g. server down, or a 500 from the search bug above).
findings.expected: Per the resilience requirement, a data page's error state should offer a retry that works once the server recovers, without a full reload.
findings.actual: On loadError the page renders only an AlertMessage with the error text and no retry control; the user must reload the page. (The plant detail journal section has the same gap for journalLoadError.)
findings.evidence: journal.vue template: <AlertMessage v-if="loadError">...</AlertMessage> with no retry button; refresh from useApiFetch is destructured but not exposed to the user. Contrast with other pages that provide retry.
